system.name: umap
system.one_liner: a memory-mapped I/O library that lets applications access files on a distributed file system as if mapped in memory, loading cache-block-sized segments on demand

components.name: APP
components.role: application process performing memory accesses to a umap-mapped file

components.name: CET
components.role: Cache Entry Table: index arrays, one per mapped file, indicating whether each file segment has been loaded

components.name: tracker
components.role: decides cache allocation/replacement based on reuse policies on a cache miss

components.name: maintainer
components.role: background thread that enacts the tracker's decisions by allocating or reusing cache blocks

components.name: Cache Set
components.role: global pool of fixed-size cache blocks (CB) that temporarily store fetched file segments

components.name: Communication Manager
components.role: merges I/O requests, manages concurrency and performs asynchronous transfers between the DFS and the local cache set

components.name: files
components.role: file segments stored on the distributed file system, divided into cache-block-sized pieces

flows.what: virtual address access intercepted and mapped to a segment index in the file's index array
data returned directly from the cache set
cache miss on the entry triggers cache-block selection
selects a CB, potentially evicting an existing one
prepares the selected CB for reuse
asynchronously fetches the required file segment from the DFS
fetched segment delivered into the prepared CB

content.key_idea: umap intercepts memory accesses to a mapped file and transparently loads only the touched cache-block-sized segments from the distributed file system on demand.
content.reading_order: Top-down: applications in user space, down through the address space and Cache Entry Table into the Cache Manager, then down to the Communication Manager and the DFS.

umap intercepts memory accesses from applications

summary: umap is a library that exposes memory-mapped I/O on a distributed file system, loading files as cache-block-sized segments on demand. The figure is a layered stack: applications (APP) in user space access a mapped address space; each access is intercepted (step 1) and looked up in the Cache Entry Table (CET). A hit returns data directly from the Cache Set (steps 2-3). A miss (step 4) invokes the Cache Manager's tracker, which selects a cache block, potentially evicting one (step 5), while the maintainer background thread prepares it for reuse (step 6). The Communication Manager then asynchronously fetches the missing segment from the underlying DFS (steps 8-9) and the CET entry is updated. Hatched fill marks address ranges currently backed by a cache block, and red hit/miss labels distinguish the two paths.
summary_zh: umap在分布式文件系统上实现按需加载的内存映射I/O:访问拦截后查CET,命中返回Cache Set数据;未命中由tracker选块、maintainer准备复用,再经Communication Manager异步从DFS取回。
